question: What is the primary role of the skin in relation to the human body?

options.B: Serving as a protective barrier against external hazards

explanation: The skin acts as the body's primary protective barrier against mechanical trauma, pathogens, radiation, and fluid loss. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why is preventive dermatology particularly significant in clinical nursing practice in Nigeria?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any pharmacological treatments
options.B: It addresses the high burden of tropical skin infections and chronic wounds
options.C: It focuses solely on cosmetic enhancements
options.D: It replaces the need for nutritional assessments

explanation: Understanding preventive dermatology is critical in Nigeria due to the high prevalence of tropical skin infections, chronic wounds, and environmental challenges. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h1)

question: Which layer of the skin provides a tough, waterproof outer barrier and continuously regenerates?
explanation: The epidermis is the outermost layer of the skin that provides a waterproof barrier and undergoes continuous cellular regeneration. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h2)

question: What is a major function of the dermal layer of the skin?

options.A: Providing structural strength, elasticity, and thermal regulation
options.B: Acting exclusively as a fat storage depot
options.D: Preventing all forms of systemic infections independently

explanation: The dermis contains connective tissue, blood vessels, and glands that offer structural strength, elasticity, and support for thermal regulation. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h2)

question: Why are harsh alkaline soaps discouraged in daily skin hygiene?

options.B: They strip away protective natural lipids, causing dryness and cracking

explanation: Harsh alkaline soaps disrupt the skin's acid mantle and strip away natural lipids, leading to dryness, irritation, and cracking. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h3)

question: When should emollients or moisturizers ideally be applied during daily hygiene routines?

options.B: Immediately after cleansing to help lock in hydration

explanation: Applying moisturizers right after cleansing helps trap moisture within the epidermal layers, preventing excessive dryness. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary effect of systemic dehydration on the skin?

options.A: Increased skin turgor and excessive oiliness
options.B: Dry, flaky skin with diminished turgor and increased vulnerability

explanation: Dehydration reduces skin turgor and causes dryness, making the skin significantly more susceptible to tears and friction injuries. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h4)

question: Which nutrient is especially essential for collagen cross-linking and acts as an antioxidant in skin repair?
explanation: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that plays a crucial role in collagen synthesis and cross-linking during tissue repair. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is a major dermatological risk associated with excessive exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation?

options.C: Sunburns, premature aging, and increased risk of skin cancers

explanation: Excessive UV radiation damages skin cells, leading to sunburns, premature aging, and a heightened risk of developing skin malignancies. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h5)

question: How can healthcare workers best protect their hands from irritant contact dermatitis caused by frequent washing?

options.B: Using appropriate PPE and applying moisturizers regularly
options.C: Washing hands exclusively with harsh chemical solvents
options.D: Scrubbing hands with abrasive brushes every hour

explanation: Wearing appropriate personal protective equipment and using moisturizers regularly helps counteract the drying and irritating effects of frequent hand hygiene. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is the primary pathological mechanism behind the development of pressure injuries?

options.B: Sustained soft tissue compression exceeding capillary closing pressure
options.C: Rapid cell regeneration in the epidermis

explanation: Pressure injuries occur when prolonged pressure over bony prominences cuts off blood supply by exceeding capillary closing pressure, leading to ischemia and necrosis. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h6)

question: How frequently should a standard immobile bedbound patient be repositioned to prevent pressure injuries?
explanation: Standard preventive guidelines recommend turning and repositioning immobile bedbound patients at least every two hours to relieve pressure on vulnerable areas. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h6)

question: What does the 'A' stand for in the ABCDE criteria used for evaluating suspicious skin lesions?
explanation: In the ABCDE criteria for melanoma detection, 'A' stands for Asymmetry, meaning one half of the mole does not match the other half. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of secondary prevention in dermatology?

options.A: Preventing the initial formation of any skin tissue
options.B: Early detection and prompt intervention to halt disease progression
options.D: Treating end-stage tissue necrosis exclusively in intensive care

explanation: Secondary prevention centers on early detection and prompt treatment to stop the progression of developing skin abnormalities or diseases. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why are individuals with diabetes mellitus considered a high-risk population for skin disorders?

options.A: They have accelerated epidermal cell turnover
options.B: They are prone to microvascular disease and delayed wound healing
options.D: They are completely immune to fungal infections

explanation: Diabetes mellitus impairs microvascular circulation and nerve function, leading to delayed wound healing and increased vulnerability to infections. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h8)

question: What is a key component of nursing care when managing high-risk populations for skin disorders?

options.A: Avoiding all physical assessments to prevent patient discomfort
options.B: Delivering rigorous daily skin assessments and tailored patient education
options.C: Discontinuing all hygiene practices to protect natural lipids
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent edema

explanation: High-risk groups require rigorous daily skin assessments, personalized care plans, and comprehensive education to prevent severe dermatological complications. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h8)
